cut_items.item: Explicitly stops running containers first with a single docker stop $(docker ps -q) before pruning, so the prune also removes the containers
Includes -f in the main command to skip the confirmation prompt, which is useful for scripting
Lists what system prune removes: stopped containers, unused images, networks, build cache, volumes
Gives docker volume prune -a -f for Docker 25+ so that named volumes are removed too
Single concise sequence: docker stop $(docker ps -q) then docker system prune -a --volumes -f, directly answering the request
Advises to back up anything needed (e.g., databases) before deleting
Follow-up command docker volume prune -a -f for when volumes remain after Engine 25+ where --volumes only removes anonymous volumes

added_items.item: Defines 'unused' as not used by a running container, so running containers and their images and volumes survive the prune unless stopped first
Docker Desktop on Mac/Windows: the disk image file does not shrink after cleanup, so use Clean/Purge data or reduce the disk image size in Settings to actually free host disk space
Gives docker builder prune -a -f to clear the build cache and docker network prune -f for networks as explicit steps
Filter example, docker image prune -a --filter until=168h, for keeping recent items
Notes that without -f, Docker prompts for confirmation
Explains that the 'requires at least 1 argument' error on empty lists is safe to ignore
States docker system prune skips named volumes unless --volumes is used, in Docker 23+
Explains that 'unused' in prune means not used by a running container (or at least a container), and that you must stop containers first to remove everything
Warns to check what you need before deleting
Explicit step-by-step full wipe including docker rm of containers (Y only mentions rm -f in the alternatives list, so mostly overlapping)
Separate cleanup of networks (docker network prune -f) and build cache (docker builder prune -a -f) as explicit commands
Notes that docker system prune asks for confirmation and -f skips it
Version note: Docker 23+ prune skips named volumes unless --volumes is given
On Docker Desktop (Mac/Windows) the disk image file doesn't shrink after cleanup; use Clean/Purge data or reduce disk image size in Settings
Filter example to keep recent items: docker image prune -a --filter "until=168h"
Explicitly states volume removal deletes database data (in the step 4 text) and that 'requires at least 1 argument' message means nothing of that type exists
